BI-S-01-FU.text: Why did you choose culinary school?

BI-S-02.text: What kind of kitchen experience do you have?

BI-S-02-FU.text: Was that school, lab, externship, or paid work?

BI-S-03.text: What do you want from your first restaurant job?

BI-S-03-FU.text: What do you hope to learn first?

FS-S-01.text: How would you introduce yourself to the chef?

FS-S-02-FU.text: What interests you about this restaurant?

FS-S-03.text: What is one strength you bring into a kitchen?

SS-S-01.text: Tell me about something you cooked that made you proud.

SS-S-02.text: Tell me about a mistake you made in culinary school.

SS-S-02-FU.text: What did you learn from it?

SS-S-03.text: Describe a time you helped a classmate in the kitchen.

SYT-S-01.text: What culinary subjects did you study?

SYT-S-02.text: What did you practice most in lab?

SYT-S-02-FU.text: How comfortable are you doing it now?

SYT-S-03.text: What did hands-on school or lab practice add to your classroom training?

SYT-S-03-FU.text: What felt most different from class?

CI-S-01.text: What does being ready for service mean to you?

CI-S-02.text: What would you do if you were given several prep tasks?

CI-S-03.text: What do you do when you do not understand an instruction?

TPP-S-01.text: How do you answer when two managers interview you together?

TPP-S-01-FU.text: Who do you look at while answering?

TPP-S-02.text: What makes you a good teammate in a kitchen?

TPP-S-03.text: How do you handle two people giving you directions?

CB-S-01.text: What would you do if you dropped something during a rush?

CB-S-02.text: What if the chef corrects you in front of everyone?

CB-S-02-FU.text: How would you react in the moment?

CB-S-03.text: What would you do if a recipe suddenly changed?

CB-S-03-FU.text: How would you avoid using the old version?

EAT-S-01.text: How do you greet a manager when you arrive?

EAT-S-02.text: How would you ask when your next shift is?

EAT-S-02-FU.text: How would you confirm the answer?

EAT-S-03.text: How would you ask a coworker for help?

EAT-S-03-FU.text: How would you thank them afterward?

FRP-S-01.text: Why do you want this job?

FRP-S-01-FU.text: Why this kitchen instead of another one?

FRP-S-02.text: What are you most ready to learn?

FRP-S-02-FU.text: Why is that important to you?

FRP-S-03.text: What would make you a reliable new hire?

FRP-S-03-FU.text: How have you shown that during training?

FI-S-01-FU.text: Is there anything that affects your availability?

FI-S-02.text: Do you have any questions for us?

FI-S-02-FU.text: What would you want to know about training?

FI-S-03.text: Is there anything else you want us to know?

FI-S-03-FU.text: What is the strongest point you want to leave us with?

BI-I-01.text: Walk me through your culinary-school training.

BI-I-01-FU.text: Which class best prepared you for a real kitchen?

BI-I-02.text: What did you learn from a school or lab kitchen assignment?

BI-I-02-FU.text: What responsibility made you improve fastest?

BI-I-03.text: What kitchen skill are you strongest at today?

BI-I-03-FU.text: Give me a specific example from school, lab, or externship.

FS-I-01.text: Why should I keep talking to you after the first minute?

FS-I-01-FU.text: What value could you bring to this kitchen quickly?

FS-I-02-FU.text: What would you change for a fine-dining kitchen?

FS-I-03.text: What do you want a chef to remember about you?

SS-I-01.text: Tell me about a dish that went wrong and how you recovered.

SS-I-01-FU.text: What did you do differently the next time?

SS-I-02.text: Describe a time your station got busy during training.

SS-I-02-FU.text: How did you decide what to handle first?

SS-I-03.text: Tell me about feedback that changed how you cook.

SS-I-03-FU.text: How did your work improve afterward?

SYT-I-01.text: How does your culinary education help you on day one?

SYT-I-01-FU.text: Which skill should require the least retraining?

SYT-I-02.text: What did lab work teach you that a textbook could not?

SYT-I-03.text: How would you explain your training without overstating your experience?

SYT-I-03-FU.text: How would you distinguish school or lab practice from paid employment?

CI-I-01.text: You are halfway through prep and falling behind. What do you do?

CI-I-01-FU.text: When do you tell the chef?

CI-I-02.text: How do you know your mise en place is actually ready?

CI-I-02-FU.text: What do you check before service starts?

CI-I-03.text: What would make you ask for help during service?

CI-I-03-FU.text: How would you ask without slowing the line?

TPP-I-01.text: Chef says speed matters; manager says consistency matters. How do you balance both?

TPP-I-01-FU.text: Which one comes first when they conflict?

TPP-I-02.text: One interviewer asks about teamwork and the other interrupts with sanitation. How do you respond?

TPP-I-02-FU.text: How do you keep both people engaged?

TPP-I-03.text: How might two instructors describe your kitchen work differently?

TPP-I-03-FU.text: What would they probably agree on?

CB-I-01.text: A cook calls out and you are moved to an unfamiliar station. What now?

CB-I-01-FU.text: What information do you need first?

CB-I-02.text: A plate comes back because the protein is overcooked. How do you respond?

CB-I-02-FU.text: What do you communicate to the line?

CB-I-03.text: The chef asks you something you genuinely do not know. What do you say?

CB-I-03-FU.text: How do you turn that into a strong answer?

EAT-I-01.text: How would you tell a manager you are running late?

EAT-I-02.text: How would you discuss your availability without sounding inflexible?

EAT-I-02-FU.text: What would you say about weekends or holidays?

EAT-I-03.text: How would you professionally disagree with a coworker?

EAT-I-03-FU.text: When should a supervisor get involved?

FRP-I-01.text: What would you contribute here during your first 90 days?

FRP-I-01-FU.text: How would we know you were progressing?

FRP-I-02.text: Why should we choose you over someone with more restaurant experience?

FRP-I-02-FU.text: What can you prove rather than promise?

FRP-I-03.text: What kind of chef do you want to become?

FRP-I-03-FU.text: What skill do you need to build next?

FI-I-01.text: If we hired you tomorrow, what would your first-week approach be?

FI-I-01-FU.text: What would you focus on before trying to impress anyone?

FI-I-02.text: What is the biggest risk in hiring you this early in your career?

FI-I-02-FU.text: How would you reduce that risk?

FI-I-03.text: What question should I have asked you but did not?

BI-BC-01.text: Imagine you have just finished a training placement. How would you prepare to help during a Saturday dinner rush?

BI-BC-01-FU.text: Now assume your assigned station is unfamiliar. What changes first?

BI-BC-02.text: Give me your strongest skill, weakest skill, and evidence for both.

BI-BC-02-FU.text: Your weakness affects tonight's prep. What is your immediate plan?

BI-BC-03.text: You're early in your kitchen career. Why hire you?

BI-BC-03-FU.text: I have another candidate with experience. Make your case.

FS-BC-01.text: You have twenty seconds. Who are you, and why this kitchen?

FS-BC-01-FU.text: I interrupt after ten seconds. Finish with one decisive point.

FS-BC-02.text: The chef looks rushed. Earn another minute without overselling yourself.

FS-BC-02-FU.text: The chef says, 'Be specific.' What do you add?

FS-BC-03.text: Open strongly without mentioning passion, dreams, or loving food.

FS-BC-03-FU.text: Now connect your opening directly to restaurant performance.

SS-BC-01.text: Describe a lab failure, your decision, and the measurable result.

SS-BC-01-FU.text: Now remove your instructor's help. What would you do alone?

SS-BC-02.text: Tell me about pressure during school or lab practice without calling yourself hardworking.

SS-BC-02-FU.text: I need one decision you made under that pressure.

SS-BC-03.text: Give me a mistake story that proves judgment, not perfection.

SS-BC-03-FU.text: The same mistake happens tomorrow. What changes immediately?

SYT-BC-01.text: Turn your culinary training into three strengths relevant to a restaurant.

SYT-BC-01-FU.text: Remove technical cooking skills. What strengths remain?

SYT-BC-02.text: Prove your lab training matters when service becomes unpredictable.

SYT-BC-02-FU.text: Now the recipe changes mid-service. Which training helps?

SYT-BC-03.text: Explain your school or lab experience accurately while still making it valuable.

SYT-BC-03-FU.text: I ask whether it was paid employment. Answer clearly.

CI-BC-01.text: Three prep tasks remain, service starts soon, and one takes twice as long. Prioritize.

CI-BC-01-FU.text: Now the chef adds an urgent fourth task. Reprioritize.

CI-BC-02.text: Your station looks ready, but one backup item is missing. Start service?

CI-BC-02-FU.text: Tickets arrive before replacement is ready. What now?

CI-BC-03.text: You are falling behind but nobody has noticed. What do you do?

CI-BC-03-FU.text: The chef says, 'Handle it yourself.' What changes?

TPP-BC-01.text: Chef asks about speed while manager asks about safety. Answer both directly.

TPP-BC-01-FU.text: They disagree with each other. How do you respond?

TPP-BC-02.text: One interviewer challenges your answer while another asks a new question. Choose your response.

TPP-BC-02-FU.text: The first interviewer interrupts again. Keep control professionally.

TPP-BC-03.text: Two managers give different priorities for your first week. What do you clarify?

TPP-BC-03-FU.text: Neither will decide. What is your next move?

CB-BC-01.text: Your station runs out of a key ingredient mid-rush. Decide fast.

CB-BC-01-FU.text: The substitute changes allergen risk. What happens next?

CB-BC-02.text: You realize you misunderstood an order after plating. What do you do?

CB-BC-02-FU.text: The table has already waited too long. What changes?

CB-BC-03.text: A teammate pushes a shortcut you believe is unsafe.

CB-BC-03-FU.text: They say everyone does it. What do you do?

EAT-BC-01.text: You need Saturday off after the schedule posts. Handle it professionally.

EAT-BC-01-FU.text: Nobody can cover you. What do you say next?

EAT-BC-02.text: A coworker keeps leaving shared prep unfinished. Address it directly.

EAT-BC-02-FU.text: They become defensive. Keep the conversation productive.

EAT-BC-03.text: Your manager gives vague criticism after service. Get useful feedback.

EAT-BC-03-FU.text: They only say, 'Be better.' What do you ask?

FRP-BC-01.text: Three interviewers ask why your limited experience is not a liability. Answer.

FRP-BC-01-FU.text: One says training is not experience. Respond without arguing.

FRP-BC-02.text: Name one reason we should hire you and one reason we might hesitate.

FRP-BC-02-FU.text: Now eliminate that hesitation with evidence.

FRP-BC-03.text: You get one minute to prove readiness for our kitchen. Go.

FRP-BC-03-FU.text: Cut your answer in half without losing substance.

FI-BC-01.text: We offer you the job, but expectations sound unclear. What do you clarify?

FI-BC-01-FU.text: The manager wants an immediate answer. What do you say?

FI-BC-02.text: You are our final candidate. Give three reasons we should choose you.

FI-BC-02-FU.text: Remove anything based only on potential. What remains?

FI-BC-03.text: Close this interview in thirty seconds without repeating earlier answers.

FI-BC-03-FU.text: I stop you halfway through. Finish with your strongest point.
